subject: Catalyst inference incident — RCA & validation checklist
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@catalyst.ai>, ops@catalyst.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst: inference availability degradation — initial readout

Lena / Catalyst team,

Thank you again for the fast signal and for working with us during the service window this morning. Quick summary up front: between 08:35 and 08:58 PDT we observed a sustained increase in per-request token latency and a partial degradation of inference throughput for your ded_alloc pool. We deployed a targeted hotfix at 09:00 PDT that restored normal throughput; our runtime telemetry shows request success returning to baseline by 09:04 PDT.

Attachments: initial timeline + deploy log. We are continuing to investigate root cause and will deliver a full RCA and an actionable validation checklist by Wednesday (timeline below).

Immediate items for you:
- Can you validate that the sample queries you shared yesterday (attached) now return expected latencies on your side? If convenient, reply with 3 representative request IDs or timestamps.
- If you still see elevated latency, please include a short curl + headers snippet and we’ll reproduce.

We are treating this as high priority; I’ve looped in Marissa and Dylan for account / escalation coordination and David for the postmortem artifacts.

Timeline:
- 08:35 PDT — first spike detected in ded_alloc pool for Catalyst (alerting fired)
- 08:40 — Ops throttle rule triggered, some requests queued, partial degradation noticed
- 08:58 — engineering rollback attempted (no change)
- 09:00 — targeted runtime patch deployed (hotfix v1.2)
- 09:04 — throughput and latency returned to baseline

We’ll follow up with the formal RCA and a validation checklist that includes the exact traces to verify, mitigations to prevent recurrence, and a verification window.

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience — we know this impacts your production workflows.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

Attachments: catalyst_initial_timeline_v1.pdf (pdf), hotfix_deploy_log_20260802.txt (text)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@catalyst.ai>, ops@catalyst.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2026 17:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Catalyst: formal RCA, timeline, actions, and verification checklist

Lena / Catalyst team — attached is the formal RCA and a short verification checklist. Summary first: root cause was an unexpected kernel selection regression in our serving runtime when handling a mid-sized batch mix under a specific sequence-length distribution. This caused a temporary kernel fallback that significantly increased per-token processing time for a subset of requests. The fallback path was not sufficiently instrumented in our alerting runbooks, so automatic mitigations were delayed.

Key points (short):
- What happened: between 08:35–08:58 PDT a small fraction (~2.7%) of in-flight requests hit a fallback execution path that increased CPU/GPU synchronization overhead, producing elevated latency and partial throughput drop for your ded_alloc pool.
- Why it happened: a kernel-selection heuristic change deployed in the previous release (2026-07-28) failed to account for a rare combination of batch-size and sequence-length that is present in your workload.
- Immediate fix: hotfix v1.2 fixed the heuristic and forced the previous stable kernel selection for affected cases (deployed 09:00 PDT).
- Missed guardrail: our alerting thresholds were tuned on aggregate p50/p95 metrics and did not escalate on the specific p99 latency pattern for this kernel-fallback case.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-08-02T15:35:12Z — first alert: increased token-level latency on ded_alloc-pool (p99)
- 2026-08-02T15:40:10Z — automatic throttling engaged; ops observed queuing
- 2026-08-02T15:58:05Z — attempted configuration rollback (no effect)
- 2026-08-02T16:00:41Z — hotfix v1.2 deployed to ded_alloc; kernel selection reverted for impacted conditions
- 2026-08-02T16:04:03Z — metrics back to baseline; monitoring shows no regression after validation window

Affected IDs / sample traces: attached sanitized list (request IDs) and trace links. We redacted PII and customer payloads per our data-sharing policy.

Actions (owners and ETA):
- Engineering (David Kim) — ship permanent kernel-selection guard that reverts to safe path when heuristic confidence is low; includes unit tests for batch/seq permutations. ETA: 2026-08-18.
- Runtime (Dylan Brooks) — add a p99-specific alert and a synthetic test in canary for the particular sequence-length distribution. ETA: 2026-08-11.
- Observability (Neha & Marissa) — add a customer-facing summary to the post-incident portal and provide Catalyst with a verification checklist + evidence bundle. ETA: delivered in this email; portal update by 2026-08-06.
- Product Ops (Marissa Cole) — propose a service credit to Catalyst for the 29-minute impact window; draft for legal and finance review. ETA: 2026-08-06.

Verification checklist for Catalyst (short):
1) Run the three representative queries you shared (attached) between 10:00–11:00 PDT and confirm p99 latency <= 350ms.
2) Share two request IDs per query if you see anomalies; we will cross-check traces and attach evidence.
3) Confirm that inference results are functionally equivalent for the queries (same model outputs); if you require, we can schedule a side-by-side comparison with our SRE.

Attachments included: catalyst_rca_detailed_v1.0.pdf (RCA with charts), catalyst_request_ids_sanitized.csv, hotfix_deploy_log_20260802.txt (deploy + rollback logs), evidence_bundle_link.txt (Drive).

Next steps: please confirm if Wed 15:00 PDT works for a 30-min verification call. We will present the mitigation plan, show post-fix telemetry, and agree on acceptance criteria for closure.

Again — apologies for the disruption. We value the partnership and want to make this as actionable and transparent as possible.

Sincerely,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
